answer: One concrete defence is to make each identity carry a slow-growing reputation that cannot be bought. A new agent starts like a vine: it must climb by doing verifiable work over time, while a glacier of accumulated attestations from independent peers backs the agents it trusts. A forge can stamp out fake identities cheaply, but it cannot stamp out a history of real contributions, cross-checks and time, so a swarm of fresh copies stays visibly shallow next to established participants.
